# Source: 常用漢字表, Cabinet Notice No. 2 of 30 November 2010
#         (平成22年内閣告示第2号), published by the Agency for Cultural Affairs:
# A cabinet notice is not a copyrighted work (Japanese Copyright Act, article 13),
# and the site allows any use of what it publishes, commercial use included, with
# Extracted from the official PDF (joyokanjihyo_20101130.pdf), in the order of
# the table, which is the order of the readings. Two liberties only: the commas
# between the examples are written 、, and a kun reading carries a dot where its
# okurigana starts (まな.ぶ), placed from the examples the table gives.
# One row per reading, 2136 kanji, 4388 readings (2352 on, 2036 kun). Columns:
#   kanji <TAB> reading <TAB> use <TAB> examples <TAB> forms <TAB> notes
# - reading: katakana for an on reading, hiragana for a kun reading.
# - use: `common`, or `narrow` for a reading the table sets back by one
#   character - "special, or of very narrow use" (法度 ハッ, a prefecture name).
# - examples: the words the table gives for that reading, separated by 、, as
#   printed: 〔副〕 and 〔接〕 mark an adverb and a conjunction, ○○ stands for a
#   name (○○岳), a reading in brackets is a sound change (三羽（ば）). Ten
#   readings have none in the table (朕 チン, 岡 おか...).
# - forms: on the first row of a kanji only, the traditional forms the table
#   prints beside it, in brackets (學). The PDF draws the one of 亀 (龜) with no
#   text behind it, and it is written in by hand. A form that differs from the
#   kanji by its glyph only (禍, 祝, and the allowed forms in square brackets)
#   has no character of its own in the text, and is left out.
# - notes: the remarks of the table about that reading, as printed. The layout
#   does not always tell two remarks of one kanji apart: those are read as one,
#   on the first of the two rows. A remark never passes to another kanji.
